column1: # One line per run of scripts/run_e2e_tests.sh (task 11.125).
# utc
# ^ Task 11.130 investigated this run. Six sign-in links did not arrive; three
#   later runs were green. WHAT WAS RULED OUT, so the next person starts here:
#   * The per-address rate limit is NOT the cause. Measured on a full 75-test
#     run on 2026-09-02: `auth_audit_log` held exactly ONE
#     rate_limit_tripped/email_limited row, and it is the deliberate probe in
#     magic_link_reader_diagnosis_e2e_test.dart. It cannot be anything else --
#     every address in this suite is minted per test by randomEmail() and gets
#     at most two requests, against a limit of three per fifteen minutes.
#     117 link_requested rows, all outcome 'sent'; no source_limited, no
#     internal_error.
#   * Accumulated old link files are NOT the cause -- task 11.118 tested that.
#   NOT RULED OUT, and not asserted either:
#   * first-run cost after container start (11.118 named it and refused to
#     assert it; this suite runs in ~8s, against a 30s per-link ceiling);
#   * clock skew between the container and the host on Docker Desktop, which
#     would make a fresh link look stale to `_isStale` and fail a random
#     minority of sign-ins. Measured on this machine: the container read
#     slightly AHEAD of the host, which is the harmless direction.
#   WHY IT COULD NOT BE SETTLED FROM THIS RUN: the reader had already asked the
#   audit log and printed a verdict for each of the six failures, and both the
#   output and the database were gone -- run_e2e_tests.sh's EXIT trap ran
#   `down -v`. That is fixed: a red run now leaves the stack up and tees its
#   output to .e2e_last_run.log.
#   ^ NOT A REAL FAILURE. Task 11.130 injected a test that calls fail() to watch
#     the red path above actually keep the stack up, rather than shipping it
#     unobserved. The probe file was deleted immediately after. Kept in the
#     ledger rather than removed, because this script did run and the count is
#     supposed to be a fact about the project; it resets the green streak, which
#     is the safe direction (11.40 counts greens, and this ledger already says
#     its count is a floor).
